Description: Mastino II della Scala, son of Alboino I, ruled Verona during its greatest territorial zenith. Conquering Padua, Vicenza, Treviso, Brescia, Parma, and Tuscan Lucca, his aggressive expansion provoked an unprecedented grand alliance between Venice and Florence to halt his hegemony. Mastino II swept across the Apennines with vast cavalry armies to subjugate Lucca and Parma, terrifying all Italy with his relentless imperial ambitions. Leading armored lancers in thunderous frontal assaults across northern Italy, his audacity forced Florence and Venice into unprecedented leagues to curb his soaring dominion. Consuming with imperial ambition, Mastino II catapulted Scaliger borders to their historic zenith, leaving an indelible imprint on Italian history despite grand coalition opposition. Throughout every bitter factional siege, imperial diet, and shifting territorial campaign across the Veneto, their relentless aristocratic dedication, strategic statecraft, chivalric discipline, steadfast valor, and immense personal resources preserve the sovereign dignity, mercantile wealth, and military supremacy of the Lordship of Verona, safeguarding civic liberty, territorial integrity, and Scaliger grandeur against every rival commune, hostile coalition, and Venetian league across northern Italy for future generations to inherit with pride, commanding profound imperial reverence from all subjects throughout Christendom and standing as an immortal beacon of chivalric honor and municipal liberty across European history.
Motivations: Push Scaliger frontiers across the Apennines to Lucca, securing maritime ports on the Tyrrhenian.
Crush Venetian mercenary armies and Florentine coalitions in pitched combat to master Italy.
Maintain vast permanent armies to cow every Italian commune through overwhelming cavalry.
Values: Believes martial force is the sole supreme law; relentless conquest alone forges immortality.
Despises political compromise as cowardice, vowing to fight against all odds.
Fears: Venetian and Florentine gold corrupting his mercenary condottieri to mutiny in mid-battle.
Being coerced into humiliating treaties that strip Parma and Lucca from his empire.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with arrogant thunder and imperial swagger, demanding unconditional submission. Always fiercely defending Scaliger dynastic authority, Veronese civic grandeur, and Veneto territorial hegemony.
